subject: Biotechnology
title: CHO Cell Culture
description: A fast breakdown of CHO Cell Culture for builders.

hook.text: Chinese hamster ovary cells produce over 70% of all biopharmaceuticals — the unsung heroes of modern medicine.

buildup.text: CHO cells grow in suspension culture — massive stainless-steel bioreactors hold up to 20,000 liters.

discovery.text: CHO cells fold human proteins correctly and add proper sugar chains — bacteria cannot do this.

twist.text: Developing a stable CHO cell line takes 6 to 12 months — finding the best producer among millions of clones.

climax.text: Modern CHO cells produce over 10 grams of antibody per liter — a 100-fold improvement in 30 years.

punchline.text: Tiny hamster cells in giant tanks — the factory behind most biologics.

quiz.question: Why are CHO cells preferred over bacteria for producing most biopharmaceuticals?
options: CHO cells grow faster than any bacterial strain
CHO cells correctly fold proteins and add sugar modifications that bacteria cannot
Bacteria are too dangerous to use in pharmaceutical manufacturing
